This quartet embodies the philosophical concept of quintessence—the fifth element beyond earth, air, fire, and water—representing the fundamental substance from which all musical reality springs.

item.title: The Connect: Community Jam — Tue Nov 10, 8:00 PM — The One Stop
item.description:
Introducing The Connect: a weekly community jam at The One Stop curated by Women to the Front on Tuesdays, 8-11pm.
Asheville Music Hall The One Stop has a long history of being a place where musicians come together. The Connect is about continuing that spirit while helping create something new. This weekly jam aims to be a welcoming, respectful space where professional musicians, rising artists, and everyone in between can come together to collaborate, connect, and learn from each other.
Each week will feature a thoughtfully curated group of musicians who will start the night with a short set and then open the night to a jam. The goal is to build community across different generations, backgrounds, genres, and levels of experience. We are committed to creating an environment where everyone can feel safe, respected, and encouraged to attend.
Come play, come listen, come make some new friends, and help us reconnect with Asheville’s music community.
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.title: Ask About Our Featured Listings — Wed Nov 11 — LiveMusicAsheville.com
item.description:
Established in February 2019, LiveMusicAsheville.com now reaches thousands of people every week actively searching for live music in the Asheville area. Roughly 60% of our traffic comes from Google Search as we dominate the top of the results for queries such as “Asheville live music” & “live music Asheville”. Meanwhile our direct traffic is experiencing explosive growth, proving more locals are now using us as their go-to music calendar. Our free listings include just the basics of Who’s Playin’ Where & When. Our Featured Listings really stand out among the dozens of events on the calendar every day. While we update every Wednesday for the following Friday thru Thursday, these Featured Listings are published much sooner and include your picture or poster, a description of the event and the venue, website/ticket links and a Google map. We also share these events on our social media stories to help further promote your show.
Source: LiveMusicAsheville.com

item.description:
Asheville Atheists Please come visit with us this Sunday November 15 to chat with like-minded people. Our new location is really working out well. It's sunny and quieter than our previous spot. We're meeting once a month on Sunday mornings. Watch your email for a specific date each month. If you think you might come, please mark Attend below; that helps us know how many tables to put together. But many have come without marking that, and that's fine. Our great new location is the cafe upstairs at Whole Foods, 4 South Tunnel Road (across from the mall). They have coffee and a lot more. Maybe you have shopping you want to do at Whole Foods or one of the other businesses on Tunnel Road before or after the meeting. We start at 10am and end at noon, but you're welcome to arrive or leave according to your own schedule. BTW - did you know our group now has over 150 members? item.title: Bluegrass and Ice Cream — Sun Nov 15, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Hendo Fun Friends Gathering on the third Sunday evening each month in the Hendersonville Presbyterian Church (HPC) community room, a crowd of up to 200 people enjoy a special blend of bluegrass and gospel music interspersed with humorous anecdotes and inspirational messages — and free ice cream and cookies to boot!
Usually fewer than 20 percent of those attending are members of HPC. The rest of the audience comes from various backgrounds, denominations and ages to hear the combination of original gospel music and old-time Southern gospel songs. A love offering for the band is taken, but giving is strictly voluntary. HPC is located at the corner of Seventh Avenue and Grove Street. Parking is in the rear of the church and accessible from Grove and King Streets and from Sixth Avenue. For more information about the church and the Bash, visit hendersonvillepc.org or call the church office, 828-692-3211.
Source: Hendo Fun Friends

item.title: Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall — Tue Nov 17, 8:00 PM — Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St.
item.description:
Every atom in your body was forged in the belly of a dying star. The calcium in your bones, the iron in your blood, the carbon threading through every strand of your DNA — all of it cooked at temperatures beyond human language, scattered across the void, and reassembled over billions of years into something that walks into a bar on a Tuesday night and listens.
Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall are four collections of stellar debris who have chosen to spend their brief window of consciousness making original music together. Not playing songs. Not running repertoire. Building something in real time from the raw material of attention, instinct, and decades of accumulated craft — compositions that didn't exist before these particular particles arranged themselves around instruments in this part...
Source: Little Jumbo

item.title: Asheville Area Job Hunters — Fri Nov 20, 1:30 PM
item.description:
AVL Digital Nomads Just getting started in job search or feeling stuck? Don't go it alone because it can be an emotional roller coaster.
Instead, join us for one, two, or all three parts of this meetup:
**1:30 pm \| The Emotional Track** *Whether you're in job search through your own choice or someone else's, the experience raises fears, hopes, and everything in between. We'll acknowledge that and help you create a mindset to move forward.*
**2:30 pm \| The Strategy Track** *Before you started job search, you had a routine. Now, it's turned upside down. We'll look at the best ways to spend your time - and more importantly help you figure out how to actually follow-through.*
**3:30 pm \| The Community Track** *Job search can be isolating. In part three of the meetup, it won't be. Share your objectives, talk about your challenges, get some new leads and ideas, and help others do the same.*
## Attendees

item.title: Jack Wilkins Quintet — Mon Nov 23, 8:00 PM — Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St.
item.description:
Jack Wilkins writes music the way a field geologist keeps a notebook. His records are named for the ground that made them. The Blue and Green Project grew out of the culture and color of the Blue Ridge. The Banff Project and The Rundle Sessions came from a Fulbright year at the University of Calgary and residencies at the Banff Centre in the Canadian Rockies. Acadian Rhythms came from his term as composer in residence at Acadia National Park, on the granite coast of Maine. One album is simply called Ridge Lines. The tenor saxophone carries all of it, a big, broad-shouldered sound that has led his University of South Florida ensembles, where he has directed jazz studies since the 1990s, to Montreux and the North Sea Jazz Festival.
This Monday brings him back toward the mountains he st...
Source: Little Jumbo

item.title: AVAS - The Acoustic Vibration Appreciation Society — Tue Nov 24, 8:00 PM — Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St.
item.description:
The Acoustic Vibration Appreciation Society starts from a simple premise: sound was here first. Strings, air, and resonating wood were moving long before anyone named the motion music, and AVAS treats that as a starting point rather than a slogan. The band began as a friendship. Jay Sanders and Jason Krekel, who had taken guitar lessons from Sanders, played their first gig together in 1991 at a student club at Hume-Fogg in Nashville. By the mid-nineties both had found their way to Boone and into the orbit of Andy Pond, whose banjo braids three-finger rolls, single-string runs, and clawhammer frailing into a single voice. In 1999 the trio recorded sixteen tracks live in West Asheville, in a studio where racks of clothing stood in for sound baffles, and the record that came out of those s...
Source: Little Jumbo

item.title: The Art of Gifting | Museum Store Sunday — Sun Nov 29, 11:00 AM — NC
item.description:
Celebrate the 10th National Museum Store Sunday at our free holiday market. You’ll find limited-time sales, including a mega-sale on West Coast glass books. There’s holiday card and ornament making, a family photo opportunity, and live harp from Lo Wolf from noon to 2pm. Orders over $100 get a free Museum tote. Museum Members always save 10% on non-consignment Museum Store items. We will also have a Member-exclusive lounge with free giftwrapping and holiday treats—available to Museum Members at no charge! The Art of Gifting | Museum Store Sunday features: Book Mega-Sale: West Coast Glass
In celebration of our current exhibition, West Coast Glass, take advantage this limited-time super sale of select Museum Store glass books, including many features on Dale Chihuly.

item.title: The Steve LaSpina New Music Ensemble — Mon Nov 30, 8:00 PM — Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St.
item.description:
Steve LaSpina learned the bass from his father in Wichita Falls, Texas, and had to wait until he was tall enough to reach the top of the upright. His father and grandfather both played in dance bands. The son carried that inheritance to Chicago, where he was working professionally by fifteen, and then to New York, where he has spent more than forty years in the company of jazz history. Marian McPartland heard him early. Benny Carter built his last working rhythm section around him after a single rehearsal. Jim Hall kept him in his trio for years, and anyone who knows Hall's playing knows what that partnership asked of a bassist: patience, space, and a sense of time that never had to announce itself.
That history matters on this particular Monday, because LaSpina arrives with two guit...
Source: Little Jumbo

Surrounding ourselves with other writers who are busy putting words onto page (physical or virtual) keeps us all accountable and focused.

item.title: Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall — Tue Dec 1, 8:00 PM — Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St.
item.description:
Every atom in your body was forged in the belly of a dying star. The calcium in your bones, the iron in your blood, the carbon threading through every strand of your DNA — all of it cooked at temperatures beyond human language, scattered across the void, and reassembled over billions of years into something that walks into a bar on a Tuesday night and listens.
Sanders, Boyd, Page & Hall are four collections of stellar debris who have chosen to spend their brief window of consciousness making original music together. Not playing songs. Not running repertoire. Building something in real time from the raw material of attention, instinct, and decades of accumulated craft — compositions that didn't exist before these particular particles arranged themselves around instruments in this part...
Source: Little Jumbo

item.title: Casey Driessen: Wednesday Bazaar — Wed Dec 2, 8:00 PM — Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St.
item.description:

Fiddle loops, wild grooves, sonic oddities, and vibrant rhythms mix together in a swirl of color and sound. Tease your tastebuds with expertly crafted cocktails and soak in the cozy, electric atmosphere. No two nights are alike—wander in, follow your ears, and see what you discover.

item.title: Chris Bullock + Justin Stanton Quartet — Mon Dec 7, 8:00 PM — Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St.
item.description:
When Snarky Puppy bandmates Chris Bullock and Justin Stanton—who've spent countless hours together since meeting in Texas in 2005—decided to bring their unique songwriting visions to Rio de Janeiro in 2023, they discovered something magical: Justin's compositions tended toward lighter sounds and feelings, while Chris's carried darker, sometimes sinister hues. The result became "Claro e Escuro" (Portuguese for "light and dark"), an album that celebrates the vibrancy of Brazilian culture while showcasing two decades of friendship, strong working rapport, and mutual respect between these five-time Grammy Award-winning multi-instrumentalists, composers, and producers.
Now these musical globetrotters bring their light-and-dark conversation to Asheville, anchored by two of the Blue Ridge's...
Source: Little Jumbo

item.title: The CORE — Mon Dec 14, 8:00 PM — Little Jumbo: 241 Broadway St.
item.description:
Consider the distances traveled to arrive at this particular room on this particular Monday night. A trumpet that has filled Madison Square Garden and the Sydney Opera House alongside Michael Bublé, now playing three feet from your cocktail glass. A baritone saxophone that has shared air with Aretha Franklin, Robert Glasper, and Ambrose Akinmusire, now threading low-register phrases through the murmur of a crowded bar. A piano that might have stayed silent forever if a freak lip injury hadn't ended a promising trumpet career and sent a political science major from Capitol Hill back to his parents' house in Nebraska to woodshed eight hours a day until his hands could do what his mouth no longer could. A bass that has crossed every ocean and touched every continent, anchored gypsy jazz an...
Source: Little Jumbo
